1What You Will Learn

  • Find documentation, whitepapers, Prescriptive Guidance, the Knowledge Center and re:Post
  • Compare the AWS Support plans: Basic, Business Support+, Enterprise Support and Unified Operations
  • Say what the Support Center, AWS Health Dashboard and Trusted Advisor are for
  • Place AWS Professional Services, solutions architects, the AWS Partner Network and AWS Marketplace

2Support, resources and partners

Running case

Tidewater Plans for Trouble

  • An outage on a busy night would need an engineer within minutes
  • The team wants guides and answers before it opens a case
  • Tidewater wants expert help to move its warehouse system, and software it can buy and deploy quickly
  • The founder wants to know when AWS itself has a problem that affects the shop
  • Your job: choose the support, resources and partners

Self-Service Help: Documentation, Guidance and Communities

Resource What you find
AWS Documentation Detailed technical guides and references for every service
Whitepapers and Guides Technical whitepapers, decision guides, reference architecture diagrams
AWS Prescriptive Guidance Guides for planning and patterns with steps, architectures and code, for migration, optimization and modernization
AWS Knowledge Center Answers to common AWS questions, hosted on AWS re:Post
AWS re:Post Community questions and answers for AWS users
AWS Trust and Safety Where to report abuse of AWS resources
  • The AWS Blogs and the AWS Architecture Center add news and designs

Exam tip: Search documentation, whitepapers and re:Post first; report abuse to Trust and Safety.

AWS Support Plans: Basic and Business Support+ Old name [Verify live]

Plan What it includes
Basic Support Included for every customer: 24/7 customer service for account and billing questions, support forums, service health checks, documentation and best practice guides, core Trusted Advisor checks
Business Support+ AI-powered, contextual help; 24/7 phone, web and chat with cloud support engineers; under 30 minutes for a business-critical system down; full Trusted Advisor checks; the Support API; third-party software help; from USD 29 a month per account
  • As of 4 November 2026: Developer Support and Business Support end on 1 January 2027; Business Support+ replaces them

Exam tip: Everyone gets Basic. Production workloads: Business Support+.

AWS Support Plans: Enterprise Support and Unified Operations [Verify live]

Plan What it adds
Enterprise Support Everything in Business Support+, plus a designated Technical Account Manager (TAM); up to 15 minutes for production-critical cases; AWS Security Incident Response; strategic reviews; AWS Countdown for critical events; USD 5,000 minimum
Unified Operations A TAM and Domain Specialist Engineers; incident managers respond within five minutes; critical workload reviews, runbooks and infrastructure event management
  • As of 4 November 2026: Enterprise On-Ramp ends on 1 January 2027, and its customers move to Enterprise Support

Exam tip: A designated TAM: Enterprise Support or Unified Operations.

Choosing a Support Plan

  • Basic Support: every customer; self-service plus account and billing help
  • Business Support+: production workloads; 24/7 engineers and full Trusted Advisor checks
  • Enterprise Support: business-critical workloads; a designated TAM
  • Unified Operations: mission-critical workloads; the fastest incident response
  • Pick the plan by how critical the workload is and how fast you need a human

Exam tip: The more critical the workload, the higher the plan; a TAM starts at Enterprise Support.

Support Center, AWS Health Dashboard and Trusted Advisor [Verify live]

  • AWS Support Center is where you open and manage support cases; Basic Support covers account, billing and service quota questions, and technical cases need a paid plan
  • AWS Health Dashboard shows ongoing visibility into AWS service availability and your resources; it needs no setup and has no additional cost
  • Health events reach you through Amazon EventBridge at no extra cost; the AWS Health API needs Business Support+, Enterprise Support or Unified Operations
  • AWS Trusted Advisor recommends ways to cut cost, and to improve performance, security and fault tolerance (Module 5)
  • As of 4 November 2026: plan details are from the Support pages

Exam tip: AWS problems that affect you: Health Dashboard. Savings and checks: Trusted Advisor.

Expert Help: AWS Professional Services, Solutions Architects and Partners

Source What it offers Think
AWS Professional Services AWS's consulting team: helps organizations design, build, migrate and manage AWS workloads Hands-on consulting
AWS solutions architects Technical guidance on designing workloads, listed in the exam guide as a technical assistance option Design advice
AWS Partners Independent software vendors, system integrators and consulting partners that build, migrate and run workloads Help from the ecosystem

Exam tip: Consulting from AWS: Professional Services. Design advice: solutions architects.

AWS Partner Network and AWS Marketplace

  • The AWS Partner Network (APN) is a global community of organizations that use AWS technologies, programs, funding and tools
  • Partners include independent software vendors (ISVs), system integrators, and consulting, training and managed-service providers
  • Benefits: training and certification, events and webinars, funding programs, co-selling with AWS and AWS Marketplace listings; the exam guide also lists volume discounts
  • AWS Marketplace is a catalog of software, data products and professional services from independent sellers, where customers find, buy, deploy and manage them, including SaaS
  • It offers private offers and some free trials (Module 5)

Exam tip: Third-party software, data or services to buy on AWS: AWS Marketplace.

What the Exam Asks: Support and Resources

  • Self-service: documentation, whitepapers, Prescriptive Guidance, the Knowledge Center and re:Post
  • Which plan: Basic for everyone, Business Support+ for production, Enterprise Support or Unified Operations for a TAM
  • AWS problems that affect you: the AWS Health Dashboard
  • Savings and checks: AWS Trusted Advisor
  • Consulting from AWS: Professional Services; design advice: solutions architects
  • Partners and software: the AWS Partner Network and AWS Marketplace
  • Abuse: AWS Trust and Safety

Exam tip: Match the need to the plan or resource: speed, a TAM, answers, consulting or software.

Design Check: Tidewater Plans for Trouble

Tidewater's need Choose

A step-by-step migration pattern AWS Prescriptive Guidance
Cloud engineers 24/7 for the production shop Business Support+
A designated TAM for business-critical launches Enterprise Support

3Exam Q&A

3.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1Tidewater's production shop needs 24/7 access to cloud support engineers, with a response in under 30 minutes for a business-critical outage, but it does not need a designated Technical Account Manager. Which plan fits best?

  • ABasic Support, which every customer receives
  • BAWS Business Support+, for production workloads
  • CAWS Enterprise Support, with a designated TAM
  • DAWS Unified Operations, for mission-critical workloads
Show the answer

Answer: B. Business Support+ gives 24/7 access to cloud support engineers and a response in under 30 minutes for a business-critical system down. Basic Support has no technical cases, and a designated TAM starts at Enterprise Support, which the shop does not need.

S2Which TWO AWS Support plans include a designated Technical Account Manager (TAM)? (Select TWO.)

  • ABasic Support
  • BAWS Business Support+
  • CAWS Enterprise Support
  • DAWS Unified Operations
  • EAWS Trusted Advisor
Show the answer

Answer: C, D. Enterprise Support and Unified Operations include a designated TAM. Basic Support and Business Support+ do not, and Trusted Advisor is a tool rather than a support plan.

S3Tidewater wants to see when an AWS service issue affects its own resources, with no setup and at no additional cost. Which service should it use?

  • AAWS Health Dashboard, which shows service and resource health
  • BAWS Trusted Advisor, which recommends cost and security improvements
  • CAWS Cost Explorer, which analyzes spending over time
  • DAWS Artifact, which provides compliance reports and agreements
Show the answer

Answer: A. The AWS Health Dashboard gives all customers ongoing visibility into service availability and resource events at no extra cost. Trusted Advisor recommends improvements, Cost Explorer analyzes spending, and Artifact provides compliance reports.

S4Tidewater wants consultants from AWS to help design, build and migrate its warehouse system. Which option fits best?

  • AAWS re:Post, which offers community answers to technical questions
  • BAWS Knowledge Center, which answers common support questions
  • CAWS Marketplace, which sells software from independent sellers
  • DAWS Professional Services, which helps design, build and migrate workloads
Show the answer

Answer: D. AWS Professional Services is AWS's consulting team for designing, building, migrating and managing workloads. re:Post and the Knowledge Center provide answers, and Marketplace is a catalog of third-party software, data and services.
